business_problem: United Imaging Healthcare needed to speed up compute-intensive MR image acquisition and reconstruction so hospitals could shorten scan times, improve image quality, and make MR procedures available to more patients.
solution_summary: United Imaging Healthcare built an AI-enabled MR imaging stack on NVIDIA accelerated computing to move reconstruction from a slow HPC bottleneck into a practical clinical workflow. Streaming sensor data from its MR systems is fed into proprietary reconstruction algorithms that run on NVIDIA data center GPUs, while the NVIDIA CUDA Toolkit is used to optimize those algorithms across environments. The team also uses cuSolver to accelerate the matrix-heavy image-reconstruction steps that previously took too long for clinical needs. NVIDIA AI Enterprise provided enterprise software support, DevTech guidance, and migration help as United Imaging product teams brought the scanner to market. Combined with the company's AI-assisted compressed sensing approach, this architecture cuts reconstruction time dramatically while preserving image quality and supporting broader access to MR imaging.

solution_components.name: NVIDIA data center GPUs
solution_components.role: Supply the accelerated compute used to run United Imaging's proprietary MR reconstruction algorithms.

solution_components.name: NVIDIA CUDA Toolkit
solution_components.role: Optimizes and deploys the MR imaging algorithms across the company's accelerated environments.

solution_components.name: cuSolver
solution_components.role: Accelerates the matrix-computation routines required for MR image reconstruction.

solution_components.name: NVIDIA AI Enterprise
solution_components.role: Provides enterprise software support and deployment assistance for the AI-enabled MR platform.

data_flow: Streaming MR sensor data enters United Imaging's proprietary reconstruction pipeline, GPU-accelerated algorithms and cuSolver process the matrix-heavy workloads, optimized CUDA-based code generates reconstructed images faster, and the results are delivered back to clinical teams with shorter patient time in the scanner.
business_outcome: United Imaging reduced MR image reconstruction time by nearly 95 percent, increased computational speed by more than 10x with additional 3x algorithm acceleration, and enabled clinical teams to shorten patient time in scanners while expanding access to MR procedures.
